items.prompt: git restore notes.md (without --staged) on a modified tracked file…
choices: Unstages the file but keeps your edits
Discards unstaged edits and matches the last committed/index state
items.explain: Plain restore rewinds the working tree; unstaged edits in that file are lost.

items.prompt: git restore --staged notes.md after git add…
choices: Removes the file from the staging area but keeps edits on disk
Deletes the file from disk forever
items.explain: restore --staged only unstages; the working tree edits remain.

items.prompt: git reset --hard is a good first choice when you only wanted to unstage one file.
items.explain: Hard reset is a last resort; prefer restore --staged or mixed reset when you want to keep file contents.

items.prompt: After restore --staged, git status on that file should show…
items.explain: Unstaged means the change is still in the working tree, just not in the index.
